before.title: Surface independence of the total current flux and the role of the displacement term
before.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), the convention of the test-geometry and divergence-theorem items cited below ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $U\cong I\times\Omega$ be the laboratory region of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $E,B$ be jointly of class $C^2$ fields of [[def-em-fields]] and $\rho,J$ of class $C^1$ source fields of [[def-em-sources]] satisfying the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on a neighbourhood of the data below.

Suppose given two patch test geometries $(D,r_1)$, $(D,r_2)$ of [[def-em-fixed-test-geometry]] over the same finite elementary Green region $D$ whose induced boundary chains coincide as oriented paths (so both patches span the same closed loop $\gamma$), and suppose there is a bounded open region $V\subseteq\Omega$ with a specified finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation whose boundary faces are exactly the two images $r_1[D]$, $r_2[D]$ with outward normals $-n_1$ and $+n_2$ respectively, where $n_i$ is the normal induced by $r_i$ (that is, $V$ is the region enclosed between the two patches; this is a hypothesis on the pair, part of its data). Then, for every $t\in I$:

(a) [Total current flux is surface independent]
$$\int_{S_1}\bigl(J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE\bigr)(\cdot,t)\cdot n_1\,dS=\int_{S_2}\bigl(J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE\bigr)(\cdot,t)\cdot n_2\,dS=\frac{1}{\mu_0}\oint_\gamma B(\cdot,t)\cdot d\mathbf r,$$
where $S_i=r_i[D]$ and the flux is that of [[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]].

(b) [Conduction-only flux need not be] For every $t\in I$ the difference of the conduction fluxes equals the negative of the difference of the displacement fluxes:
$$\int_{S_1}J(\cdot,t)\cdot n_1\,dS-\int_{S_2}J(\cdot,t)\cdot n_2\,dS=-\varepsilon_0\left(\int_{S_1}\partial_tE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_1\,dS-\int_{S_2}\partial_tE(\cdot,t)\cdot n_2\,dS\right).$$
Hence the conduction-only fluxes are equal exactly when the displacement fluxes are equal, and neither conclusion is forced by the Maxwell equations alone.

(c) [Explicit realisation] The following declared smooth data satisfies all the hypotheses above and has different conduction fluxes through the two surfaces. On $\Omega=\mathbb R^3$, $I=\mathbb R$, fix $\chi\in C^\infty(\mathbb R)$ with $0\le\chi\le1$, $\chi(z)=1$ for $z\le-1$ and $\chi(z)=0$ for $z\ge0$, and set
$$E(x,t):=\frac{t}{\varepsilon_0}\chi(z)\,e_z,\qquad B:=0,\qquad \rho(x,t):=t\,\chi'(z),\qquad J(x,t):=-\chi(z)\,e_z.$$
Then $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=0=-\partial_tB$, $\operatorname{curl}B=0=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$ (the last identity because $c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}=\mu_0$), and $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$. Take $D=[-1,1]^2$, let $\eta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$ with $0\le\eta\le1$, $\eta=1$ in a neighbourhood of the origin and $\eta=0$ on $\partial D$, and take the graphs
$$r_1(u,v):=(u,v,-2\eta(u,v)),\qquad r_2(u,v):=(u,v,0).$$
Both induced boundary chains are the square $\{(u,v,0):(u,v)\in\partial D\}$, the region $V=\{(u,v,w):-2\eta(u,v)<w<0\}$ is enclosed between the patches, and
$$\int_{S_1}J\cdot n_1\,dS=-\int_D\chi(-2\eta(u,v))\,dudv<0,\qquad \int_{S_2}J\cdot n_2\,dS=-\int_D\chi(0)\,dudv=0,$$
the first inequality because $\eta=1$ in a neighbourhood of the origin, so $\chi(-2\eta)=1$ on a nonempty open subset of $D$, whose area is positive.
while both total current fluxes in (a) vanish, consistently with the loop integral $\oint_\gamma B\cdot d\mathbf r=0$. In the standard charging-capacitor discussion the two spanning surfaces cut the conduction current in different ways and the difference is carried by the displacement term; the realisation above exhibits exactly this phenomenon in a self-contained smooth model. An idealised thin-wire current is not a source type of this framework and the capacitor interpretation is explanatory, not an additional empirical claim.
before.strategy: (a) Put $G:=J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE$, of class $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of $\overline V$. By the smooth Gauss law and [[thm-clairaut-schwarz-mixed-partials]], $\operatorname{div}G=\operatorname{div}J+\varepsilon_0\partial_t\operatorname{div}E=\operatorname{div}J+\partial_t\rho=0$ on that neighbourhood, the last equality being continuity, [[pthm-em-charge-continuity]](a). [[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-piecewise-c-one-domains]] applied to $G$ on the specified presentation of $V$ — outward normal $-n_1$ on the face $S_1$ and $+n_2$ on the face $S_2$ — gives $0=\int_V\operatorname{div}G=\int_{S_2}G\cdot n_2-\int_{S_1}G\cdot n_1$, which is the first asserted equality. The equality with $(1/\mu_0)\oint_\gamma B\cdot d\mathbf r$ is Ampere's integral identity of [[pthm-em-integral-maxwell]](a) applied to either patch, whose induced boundary chain is $\gamma$; the two patches consequently give the same circulation. (b) Split $G$ in the equality of (a); this is algebra with the definitions of the fluxes ([[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]], [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]) and no further analytic input. (c) Verify the smooth equations for the displayed data by direct substitution: $\operatorname{div}E=(t/\varepsilon_0)\chi'(z)$ and $\operatorname{div}B=0$; $\operatorname{curl}E=\operatorname{curl}(E_z(z,t)e_z)=0$ because $E_z$ is independent of $x$ and $y$, so $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB=0$; $\operatorname{curl}B=0$ and $\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE=-\mu_0\chi(z)e_z+c^{-2}\varepsilon_0^{-1}\chi(z)e_z=0$ since $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$; and $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=\chi'(z)-\chi'(z)=0$. The graphs $r_1,r_2$ are smooth patches of class $C^\infty$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]] over the rectangle $D$ (a finite elementary Green region, [[def-type-i-type-ii-and-elementary-green-regions]]); since $\eta=0$ on $\partial D$, both induced boundary chains are the square at height zero ([[def-the-induced-boundary-chain-of-a-c2-surface-patch]]). The enclosed region $V$ has the two graph faces as its boundary with the outward normals $-n_1$ and $+n_2$, and its presentation is the finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation required by the statement, with the seam over $\partial D$ as edge set. For the fluxes, $(F\circ r)\cdot(r_u\times r_v)$ with $r_u\times r_v=(-\varphi_u,-\varphi_v,1)$ gives $J\cdot n_i=-\chi(\varphi_i)$ for a graph $w=\varphi(u,v)$ ([[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]]); with $\varphi_1=-2\eta$, $\varphi_2=0$ and $\chi$ as chosen, the second integral is zero because $\chi(0)=0$, and the first is strictly positive: $\eta=1$ on a ball $B(0,r)\subseteq D$, so $\chi(-2\eta)=1$ there, and the Riemann integral over the compact Jordan region $D$ of the nonnegative continuous integrand dominates $\lambda_2(B(0,r))>0$ after the Riemann-to-Lebesgue comparison ([[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], [[lem-euclidean-balls-have-positive-finite-lebesgue-measure]], [[thm-monotonicity-of-the-integral]]). The total fluxes both vanish because $G=J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE=-\chi(z)e_z+\chi(z)e_z=0$, consistent with the vanishing circulation of $B=0$. The bump $\eta$ is supplied by [[lem-scaled-euclidean-bumps-with-compact-support-and-gradient-bound]]; the marked $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the convention of the test-geometry, surface-measure and divergence-theorem items, and no further choice is used.

before.physical_scope: The surface-choice structure of the classical electromagnetic framework in a named inertial laboratory frame: for two oriented patches sharing a boundary loop and enclosing a region, the flux of the total current density $J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE$ is the same through either patch and equals the circulation of $B$ divided by $\mu_0$, whereas the conduction-only flux may differ, its difference being carried by the displacement term; a self-contained smooth realisation is exhibited. The item is a conditional deduction from the adopted Maxwell equations and their continuity consequence; it asserts no experiment, no apparatus and no measurement, uses no idealised thin-wire current, and carries the declared $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of the test-geometry and divergence-theorem items.

The standard step is smooth, is zero for arguments at most zero, is one for arguments at least one and is strictly positive on $(0,1)$ ([[def-the-standard-smooth-step-function]]). Thus $h$ is smooth, positive for $|s|<1$, one for $|s|\le1/\sqrt2$ and zero for $|s|\ge1$; the product $\eta$ has exactly the declared properties. In particular the entire open square has positive graph separation, rather than merely a central subregion. Both graph maps are smooth and injective regular parametrizations on a neighbourhood of $D$, since their first two coordinates are $(u,v)$ and their area vectors are $(-\varphi_u,-\varphi_v,1)$. Their induced square boundary chains coincide at height zero. The explicitly restricted $V$ is nonempty, bounded and open, with compact closure contained in $[-1,1]^2\times[-2,0]$; its boundary is exactly $S_1\cup S_2$. Strict positivity of $\eta$ on $D^\circ$ gives $S_1\cap S_2=\partial D\times\{0\}$. This square seam is a compact union of four line segments, has surface measure zero on each regular graph face, and contains the relative face boundaries. At every point off the seam the boundary is locally the single smooth graph with $V$ above the lower graph and below the upper graph. The faces therefore give the actual finite presentation of [[def-bounded-piecewise-c-one-euclidean-domain]], with outward normals $-n_1,+n_2$, without overlapping positive-area face pieces. For $\varphi_1=-2\eta$, the induced upward unit normal is $n_1=(2\eta_u,2\eta_v,1)/\sqrt{1+4|\nabla\eta|^2}$, so $(J\circ r_1)\cdot n_1=-\chi(-2\eta)/\sqrt{1+4|\nabla\eta|^2}$; after multiplication by its area Jacobian the pullback density is $(J\circ r_1)\cdot(r_{1,u}\times r_{1,v})=-\chi(-2\eta)$. For the plane $n_2=e_z$ and the density is $-\chi(0)=0$. The graph flux formula thus gives exactly the two stated integrals, with the unit-normal scalar distinguished from the unnormalized area-vector density. On any ball $B(0,r)$ with $0<r<1/2$, $\eta=1$ and $\chi(-2\eta)=1$. The nonnegative continuous integrand has strictly positive integral on $D$, by the Riemann/Lebesgue comparison, monotonicity and positive ball area already declared; its negative is the strictly negative lower conduction flux, as stated. The total fluxes both vanish because $G=J+\varepsilon_0\partial_tE=-\chi(z)e_z+\chi(z)e_z=0$, consistent with the vanishing circulation of $B=0$. The explicit step-product supplies the required positivity on the entire square interior; the marked $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is the convention of the test-geometry, surface-measure and divergence-theorem items, and no further choice is used.
